short_description: A streaming service bought a 420-title library whose vendor metadata is so thin that tag-driven home rows and search barely show it (30% of the catalogue, 10% of impressions) — and some titles sit in the kids row with no content warnings. AI Functions read every title's scenes and propose genres, moods, themes, keywords, a synopsis and evidence-backed content warnings on a governed taxonomy; the Standards Guide is applied as code and cited by the Genie agent from the guide's documents; Vector Search finds look-alikes and promo clips; editors publish the change from a Databricks App on Lakebase with an audit trail, while content strategy tracks the discovery gap and the re-tag lift in an AI/BI dashboard and Genie.
